Bayley - who commuted from Scotland to be at every League match, Pat Lyttle; Snowy - now back in the BL after 10 years; Terry Welsh - our remaining resident Irish Guard;Paul Whitby - who intends to commute from Scotland next season.
Snowy made a welcome return and boosted our field team. We now have four big men capable of beating the best and it was good to see Field Captain John Aska keeping everybody on their toes.

Other winners included Stu Paton (800), Steve Samson (PV) Terry Welsh (HT), Snowy (JT). John Aska did his usual great work organising the field side and surprised himself and everybody else, with his largest javelin throw for some time of 53.84.
Thanks to a second dress rehearsal for Trooping the Colour, we could not call on any of our guards and with Snowy also unavailable we were very weak in the throws.
The other stars on the day were Mark in the P.V. Derek 400, LJ; Snowy SP and the announcer's nightmare!
Derek Williams was at his brilliant best as were Ken, Snowy, Vincent, Mark and sprinters Pat Lyttle and Mike Alleyne. Benny did his usual trick in the B 800 of being last with 200 to go.

John Bicourt won the S/C in 9:05.5 a brilliant run for a 38 year old youngster! Neil Phillips won the 'B' discus as did Snowy in the 'B' shot. A great day with the Bels. still on the up - Div. 3 next year!

But even with Abi and Snowy winning both strings of the discus, the boys from the South Coast won the day. 100m: 3, S.Dominetti 11.9; 1, J.Carr 11.8. 200m: 2, S.Dominetti 23.5; 1, J.Carr 23.8. 400m: 2, D.Winson 53.8; 2, M.Chuter 54.8. 800m: 3, N.Clarke 2:01.2; 2, M.Bowers 2:07.0. 1500m: 4, N.Clarke…
